title: SRE-first evaluation criteria for managed AI endpoints
content:
Purpose:
This note is a go-to-market messaging brief aimed at SRE and platform engineering buyers who prioritize operational reliability, observability, and incident readiness when evaluating managed AI endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure style). It maps the SRE evaluation checklist to Redwood-specific win themes, expected objections, demo hooks, and suggested conversational scripts for AE/SEs.

Audience framing (one-sentence):
Platform/SRE leads evaluate managed AI endpoints through the lens of system-level SLAs, predictable failure modes, deterministic fallbacks, and low cognitive overhead for incident response. Position Redwood as the option that treats inference like a first-class production system rather than a best-effort ML playground.

Topline SRE evaluation axes (what they actually test in a POC):
- Availability & Recovery: scheduled maintenance impact, pod/instance churn, multi-AZ failover.
- Latency SLOs & Tail Behavior: p95/p99 latencies under steady-state and burst traffic, cold-start characteristics.
- Error Modes & Observability: triage artifacts (traces, token-level timing), meaningful error categories, root-cause signals.
- Degraded-mode behavior: graceful fallback to smaller models or cached responses, admission controls.
- Throughput & Backpressure: how system signals and throttles when queues/backlog increase.
- Determinism & Repro: reproducible runtimes for identical requests (seeded runs, model pinning).
- Security & Isolation: tenancy isolation guarantees, VPC/on-prem connectivity, KMS integration.
- Operational ergonomics: runbooks, runbook automation, alert noise, and run frequency.

How hyperscalers typically show up on these axes (short):
- AWS/GCP/Azure: strong on raw capacity and region reach; operational primitives (LBs, zones) and SLAs for infra, but endpoint-level behavior can be opaque (managed autoscaling black boxes, limited token-level telemetry). Fallbacks are typically customer-built.

Redwood win themes mapped to SRE axes (concise bullets):
- Predictable degraded-mode: Configurable automatic fallbacks (model variants, cached prefixes) and transparent policies that preserve responses instead of returning 500s.
- Token-level observability: traceable per-token latency and cost breakdowns surfaced in Console and exportable to tracing backend (Sentry/Datadog).
- Deterministic rollouts and pinning: model version pinning and A/B rollout controls to make canaries reproducible for incident correlation.
- Clear operational controls: fine-grained admission and burst policies (per-route) plus backpressure behavior that’s observable and tunable.
- Private deployment parity: same API and tooling for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) so SREs can maintain familiar runbooks across cloud and private infra.

Common SRE objections and short counters (for SEs):
- "Hyperscaler is simpler, we already use AWS/GCP for infra": Redwood: "We integrate with your cloud infra but expose inference primitives and telemetry hyperscalers don’t surface. You get cloud reach plus deterministic inference controls."
- "Managed endpoints go down unexpectedly": Redwood: "We bake fallback variants and cached prefixes into default routing policies; in POC we show how a region or model outage results in warm fallback within X ms instead of 5xxs."
- "We need full stack visibility": Redwood: "We provide token/timing traces, request correlation IDs that link runtime events to logs and traces in your observability backend; plus exportable diagnostics for postmortems."
- "Cost spikes during incidents": Redwood: "Routing policies and burst limits allow you to prioritize critical routes and shed best-effort traffic automatically; Optimize suggests quantization/batching profiles to reduce per-token cost."

POC checklist / playbook (what to run in a 2-week SRE-led eval):
Week 0: setup
- Provision a sandbox tenant on Redwood Hosted + a Private VPC staging deploy (if needed).
- Ingest representative traffic (synthetic generator + real replayed requests).
- Establish baseline: p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, token cost per request.

Day 1–3: failure injection & tail testing
- Introduce simulated model eviction and region failover. Observe routing, fallback time, and error surface.
- Measure tail latencies with burst traffic patterns. Pin models and reproduce canary results.

Day 4–7: observability & triage exercises
- Trigger degraded behavior and perform a full postmortem exercise with exported traces.
- Validate token-level breakdowns and automatic alert thresholds.

Day 8–12: admission control & cost controls
- Configure per-route admission and set burst/cutoff policies. Exercise shed behavior under overload.
- Run Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization) and measure cost/latency tradeoffs.

Deliverables for SRE POC sign-off:
- Runbook draft for common incidents (model OOM, instance preemption, region outage) with steps referencing Redwood Console actions.
- Side-by-side metrics: p99 latency heatmaps and cost per 1M tokens across conditions.
- A short incident replay demo: show fail->fallback->recover sequence in under 60s.

Demo hooks (what to show during a 20–30 minute SE demo):
- Live token-level latency trace for a single request, showing where time is spent (network, KV cache, kernel).
- Triggering a canary rollback with model pinning and showing identical request deterministic outputs before/after.
- Simulate a node preemption and show automatic routing + cached response hit.
- Console: per-route SLO dashboard with alerting integration to PagerDuty/Slack.

Suggested one-liners and email subject lines for outreach to SRE leads:
- Subject: "Runbooks that actually work for AI endpoints — quick POC for your SRE team"
- Opening line: "If you treat inference like a production service, Redwood gives you the control and telemetry missing from cloud-managed endpoints — predictable fallbacks, token-level traces, and private deployment parity."

Measuring success (POC KPIs SRE cares about):
- p99 latency under burst vs baseline (target: <= baseline + 20ms)
- Mean time to fallback (target: < 2s from detected failure to degraded output)
- Reduction in 5xx rate during simulated infra failures (target: 90% fewer 5xx vs hyperscaler baseline)
- Number of noisy alerts during the test window (target: <= existing alert volume)
- Cost delta for 1M tokens under production traffic patterns (goal: <= 10% worse or cost-neutral with clear latency benefits)

Risks and internal talking points to prep for sales cycles:
- If the customer insists on hyperscaler-managed autoscale as the single criterion, position Redwood as complementary: "use hyperscaler infra, but run inference through Redwood to gain operational parity and control."
- For customers anchored on lowest per-token list price: emphasize unit economics under typical production patterns and show Optimize suggestions that materially reduce per-token cost.

Open questions (for product/engineering follow-up):
- Can we produce a pre-built SRE-runbook template for the POC that wires default PagerDuty/Slack integrations?
- Can we capture a compact incident replay artifact that SEs can play during demos without requiring full customer traffic replay?
- What exact p99 SLA wording can we offer for Dedicated contracts related to degraded-mode behavior?

Appendix: example incident runbook excerpt (short)
- Symptom: sudden spike in 5xxs for route api/v1/generate
  1) Check Console -> Route -> Recent Traces for increased network vs runtime time.
  2) If runtime OOMs detected, switch route to fallback model variant (Console -> Rollouts -> Activate fallback).
  3) If region outage, toggle route routing policy to prefer other regions (or activate Private fallback).
  4) Export traces to SRE team and label incident for postmortem with correlation ID.

Notes to SEs: avoid generic "we’re more reliable" claims. Use measurable comparisons (fallback latency, reduction in 5xxs, traceable token-level timelines). Bring a short runbook and the POC checklist to the first SRE meeting.

Author notes:
- Drafted for internal validation before making a public one-pager. Would like engineering input on exact fallback timings and a sample runbook template to attach to the POC artifact.
